set.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, New or Old Army Pass, or Arc Pass; camping is good anywhere in the basin. The Miter is the two-headed peak between the Sky Blue Lake and Iridescent Lake basins. Janitorial Service is on the north summit; from Sky Blue Lake, go uphill eastward to the middle of its west face.
set.descent_text: Unrope on top of the final short pitch, scramble to the summit, and descend by the Northwest Chute, which is the easiest way up or down the peak.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page and the Northwest Chute page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, New or Old Army Pass, or Arc Pass; camping is good anywhere in the basin. The Miter is the two-headed peak between the Sky Blue Lake and Iridescent Lake basins. The Miterhorn takes the west arete of the south summit. Head toward the long splitter corner, then traverse left around it to a pedestal that marks the foot of the arete.
set.descent_text: After the south summit, traverse over to the true north summit and descend the Northwest Chute, which is the easiest way up or down the peak.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page and the Northwest Chute page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Take the Sphinx Creek Trail toward Avalanche Pass and work over to the gully on the east side of the formation. Descend that gully, a class 3-4 scramble, to a ledge close to the lowest part of the east face, where the route starts.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: The formation is visible from the bottom end of the Bubbs Creek Trail and on the hike to Mist Falls from Roads End. For the short summit routes, follow the Sphinx Creek Trail toward Avalanche Pass, ford Sphinx Creek, and climb the slope east of the Sphinx without a trail. A longer, easier alternative continues south along the trail before turning north uphill, with some elevation lost to reach the starts. North Buttress climbs the sub-summit's north side; reach its base by going down the northwest ridge from the summit and then traversing across to the route's foot.
set.descent_text: Get down to the saddle separating the sub-summit from the true summit, by downclimbing or rappelling, climb the short dihedral to the top of the true summit, then retrace the approach.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: The formation is visible from the bottom end of the Bubbs Creek Trail and on the hike to Mist Falls from Roads End. South Side climbs the sub-summit from the notch between the two summits: from the true summit, downclimb or rappel to the notch, locate a ledge beneath it, and follow the ledge to its far end.
set.descent_text: Reverse the route by downclimbing, or leave rappel gear on the sub-summit. Getting back up from the notch to the true summit means climbing the single short dihedral.

set.approach: The crag is a buttress on the left side of the glaciated bowl under Tuolumne Peak's southeast face. It is a long cross-country trip from May Lake or from Polly Dome Lakes. Fun begins at a pair of cracks next to the arete at the right-hand limit of the climbing.
set.descent_text: Climb or scramble off to the right.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route and wall pages. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Walk the trail into Little Slide Canyon. Just before the trail fords the creek, turn off and grind up talus to the formation's foot. Another option is to stay on the main trail until the rock benches end, then curve east around the marsh and climb talus. Gambit shares its first pitch with Silver Surfer.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the bolted anchor under the summit block. Drop over the west flank into the first gully on your right, keep left of the tower in that gully, and make one further rappel from bolts over a chockstone before walking back to the base.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route and wall pages. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: The Thunderbird Wall is reached from the foot of the Claim Jumper Wall by a brief trail and some scrambling, and a similar link comes in from the neighbouring Gunsmoke Wall. The wall faces east, toward both of those walls. Sugarloaf lies downhill and to the left of High Plains Drifter, at the east face's left edge.

set.approach: From the Tuttle Creek trailhead, walk the old dirt road to the Ashram stone house, then continue up the North Fork of Tuttle Creek on a faint, cairned trail on the south side of the drainage. After a long stretch the cairned path comes close to the base of the slab. Leave it where it looks good and scramble straight up to the base. Jim's Buttress runs up the left margin of the big steep buttress on the canyon's south flank.
set.descent_text: Descend the slopes on the right side (looking up) back to the approach path.

set.approach: Take the Tuttle Creek trail to the Ashram, then turn left onto a sandy sidehill path that reaches the South Fork of Tuttle Creek, and go up the drainage, looking for cairns. When the ground is clear of snow, keep north of the creek for more than half the distance, passing Keyhole Wall on your right, and cross at a meadow; with snow, cross to the south side sooner. Stay with the creek until it runs directly under the wall, below the Obelisk. Basecamp Hearsay starts at the foot of the long squeeze chimney inside the big dihedral, the dominant feature of the wall.
set.descent_text: From the top, climb the talus toward the Obelisk until the slabs on your right are behind you, then traverse east toward trees and continue to a point where ledges allow downclimbing. Go down the lower talus to the foot of the wall.
